root_cause.text: The bounds check for 128-byte SQE operations validated the logical SQ head position instead of the physical SQE index, allowing unprivileged users to bypass the check by remapping logical positions to arbitrary physical indices via sq_array.
root_cause.evidence: The original check `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))` only validates the logical position in the ring buffer. When `sq_array` is present, users can set `sq_array[N] = sq_entries - 1` to place a 128-byte operation at the last physical SQE slot, causing the subsequent 128-byte memcpy in `io_uring_cmd_sqe_copy()` to read 64 bytes past the end of the SQE array. The fix replaces this with a direct physical index validation: `(unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1`, which correctly checks the actual physical SQE pointer position regardless of sq_array remapping.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix SQE boundary validation to correctly detect insufficient space for 128-bit mixed SQ operations by checking actual offset bounds instead of cached head alignment.
intent_record.what: Replaced the condition `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))` with `(unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1` in the boundary check for SQE (submission queue entry) validation.
intent_record.how: The original condition checked if cached_sq_head was not aligned to the SQ entries boundary using a bitmask operation. The new condition directly validates that the computed SQE offset does not exceed or equal the maximum allowed entries minus one, providing a more explicit and semantically correct bounds check for detecting when there is insufficient space for a 128-bit (2-entry) operation.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the SQE boundary validation logic. It changes from checking the logical SQ head position (which could be bypassed via sq_array remapping) to checking actual offset bounds, which correctly validates the physical SQE index regardless of how logical positions are mapped.

candidates.rationale: This bounds check validates ctx->cached_sq_head (logical SQ head position) instead of the actual physical SQE index. The check '!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))' only verifies alignment of the cached head, not whether there is sufficient physical space in the SQE ring. An attacker can remap logical positions to arbitrary physical indices via sq_array, bypassing this check.

This specific condition checks only the alignment of the cached_sq_head against sq_entries, which is a logical position check. It fails to validate the actual physical offset bounds needed for 128-byte SQE operations, allowing the vulnerability where logical positions can be remapped to arbitrary physical indices.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition checks only the alignment of cached_sq_head (logical SQ head position) against sq_entries, rather than validating the actual physical SQE index bounds. It fails to detect when the physical SQE index lacks sufficient space for 128-byte operations, allowing attackers to bypass the bounds check by remapping logical positions to arbitrary physical indices via sq_array.
